findings.description: [qodo] _annotate_hunks duplicates line prefixes (+ and -). In unidiff, line.value already starts with '+' for additions or '-' for deletions. Prepending '+' in '[+%4d] +%s' or '-' in '[----] -%s' results in double prefixes like '++added1' and '--removed1'.

[qodo] _extract_file_mode slices diff_text from 'diff --git' to ' b/<filepath>', producing a chunk containing only 'diff --git a/<filepath>'. Because 'new file mode' / 'deleted file mode' lines occur after 'b/<filepath>', re.search always fails and returns the default '100644'.

[expert] `_extract_file_mode` creates `chunk = diff_text[start:pos]` where `pos` is the index of ' b/filepath' in the 'diff --git' line. Because the mode specification ('new file mode ...' or 'deleted file mode ...') appears on a subsequent line after 'b/filepath', `chunk` only contains 'diff --git a/filepath' and excludes the mode line. `re.search` will always fail to match, causing `_extract_file_mode` to consistently return the default '100644'.

[adversarial] In _annotate_hunks, line.value in unidiff already contains the diff prefix (+, -, or space). Prepending '+' or '-' to raw (line.value.rstrip('\n')) produces double prefixes ('++' and '--') on added and removed lines, corrupting the annotated diff.

[adversarial] In _extract_file_mode, pos is computed as diff_text.find(' b/%s' % filepath), which points to the header line diff --git. Slicing diff_text[start:pos] ends before the 'new file mode' / 'deleted file mode' line, so regex searching pattern in chunk will always fail and fall back to '100644'.
